chunks.text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are advanced AI systems trained on massive datasets to understand and generate human-like text. They are widely used in applications such as chatbots, document search, summarization, and code generation.

Most modern LLMs are based on the transformer architecture, which uses attention mechanisms to process sequences of text efficiently. This architecture enables parallel computation and better contextual understanding.

The attention mechanism allows the model to focus on relevant words in a sentence when generating responses. Self-attention is a key innovation that improves performance in natural language processing tasks.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines external knowledge retrieval with language model generation. This approach improves factual accuracy by grounding responses in retrieved documents.
Document chunking is the process of splitting large documents into smaller segments. Hierarchical chunking uses headings and structure to create logical sections for indexing and retrieval.
Embeddings convert text into numerical vectors that capture semantic meaning. Vector databases store these embeddings and enable similarity search for efficient information retrieval.
